title: Literally turned me into a coffee drinker. Easy to use, easy to clean, and the milk froth is fluffy
text:
Literally turned me into a coffee drinker. Easy to use, easy to clean, and the milk froth is fluffy. [[VIDEOID:c0970f8faeb3219291fd414d42b0a60e]]
***Reduced to 3 Stars for magnet failure April 2, 2018****

Two weeks and the machine stopped working. It kept flashing a red warning that the bean hopper door was open even when it was obviously closed. No way to get past the warning and make coffee. I searched online and found out that this is a known, ongoing problem in these Saeco machines involving a cheap plastic part and a magnet. I carefully pulled every single coffee bean out of the hopper and the opening to the grinder and found two things mixed in with the beans - a tiny magnet and a piece of plastic that had snapped off the hopper door edge!! See the photos.

I was able to slip the magnet back in place and the machine works now, however....in order to stop this from happening again, I have to very slowly open the hopper, ensure the magnet is still in place, put a finger over it and then add new beans and slowly close the door over the magnet. Seriously??? A four figure price tag and it has plastic parts snapping off and falling into the coffee beans - ridiculous. Philips is the parent company here and they darn sure need better quality control.

****** ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW*****

Historically, I dislike coffee - it always tastes bitter and burned to my palate unless it's mixed into one of those pricey store bought milkshake things. My husband though has always been a coffee guy so I chose this espresso machine primarily for his benefit. As it turns out, I'm completely hooked on it and use it multiple times a day.

This machine is really attractive and looks nice in our kitchen and it fits perfectly in the spot the old Kuerig used to live (that thing and the K- cups are outta here!) The initial setup took me about 40 minutes plus another 20 minutes reading the book cover to cover and breaking the machine down so I could fully understand how it works. Only then did I try making a beverage and I haven't stopped since in a week. Heck, I'm drinking a chocolate cappuccino as I type this.

The bean hopper holds a lot of coffee beans and feeds them directly into the grinder and brews a cup of magic. The used grounds fall into a container in tight little circles to be disposed of later. Making a coffee that even I will love has proven astonishingly simple and consistent and that amazes me. The milk steamer/frother thingy is the reason. It's best with ice cold milk straight out of the fridge - also, chocolate milk works in it and makes a chocolate latte to die for! I'm sure coffee afficianados already know that trick, but as a first timer it was the best little surprise. (We drink only real, natural whole cow milk - no fake vegetable oil "milk like" stuff, so I can't speak to how the steamer works there.)

You can select the brew strength and type of drink you want from a super strong little espresso or cafe crema, to a mid strength full size cappuccino with a very light, fluffy foam that you can swirl a design in. My husband and my mother are very happy with the traditional versions and both prefer a very strong coffee from a dark roast bean. I'm incredibly happy with the light roast and a low medium strength with hot milk and a dash of sugar. It makes great tasting coffee with simple, generic beans too - so far we've been using an Amazon Basics dark roast bean and a light roast Columbian bean under the Wally world label, both costing less for two pounds of beans than a latte at a coffee shop.

You definitely want to keep an empty mug under the spouts when your made coffee is finished - the machine does a quick rinse off the milk nozzle and before it goes into sleep mode, it rinses the coffee nozzle. Because it's actually fresh grinding the beans, it's loud as it starts your drink - you aren't going to sneak around making cappuccino at 5am, you better plan on sharing with whomever you wake up. Bottom line is that the Picobaristo is reasonably easy to get the hang of for a first time user and it is simple to operate even half asleep at 5:30am.
